subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw repair from canonical peer data and otherwise drop before access control, or only apply a narrower peer repair?
rationale: The repaired sender becomes the authorization subject and reply route, so the permanent behavior is a security and message-delivery boundary rather than a purely local refactor.

options.title: Require Canonical Repair And Fail-Closed
options.body: Repair only when the peer is canonicalization-distinct from the local sender, otherwise drop before access control and cover both cases with tests and live proof.

options.title: Accept Narrow Repair Only
options.body: Merge a canonicalized peer repair without a new fail-closed branch, while accepting that unresolved local-sender payload shapes may continue downstream.

options.title: Pause For Separate Root Cause
options.body: Leave this draft paused until the author or a maintainer isolates whether the remaining failure is this race or a different iMessage identity bug.

recommendation.title: Require Canonical Repair And Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Repair only when the peer is canonicalization-distinct from the local sender, otherwise drop before access control and cover both cases with tests and live proof.
